title: AM-MultiModal-Monitoring: an integrated in-situ monitoring system for metal additive manufacturing with a detectability bound
description:
Code and documentation for a multi-modal in-situ monitoring system for laser powder-bed fusion and directed energy deposition, extended with a closed-form bound on what any detector could achieve given the sensing chain.

The system has two halves. A measurement chain classifies process state from acoustic emission, laser ultrasound, and phase / point-cloud data, using a unified Kalman fusion framework with offline edge intelligence. A decision layer states the ceiling of that chain: for a known signal in additive noise the matched filter maximises the deflection, so detection probability cannot exceed Phi(d' - z) whatever the model, and the geometry of the flaw enters through a single energy functional with two asymptotes.

Provenance is a first-class property. A machine-generated registry of 28 analysis stages tags each one as measured (7), simulated (9) or derived (12), and the reporting layer refuses to merge the categories, so a simulated fusion result cannot be quoted as process evidence. The registry is produced from the source by a scanner and a test asserts that the two agree, so it cannot drift.

Contents: the analysis scripts that produced the published figures, the orchestration package (registry, pipeline, decision layer, reporter, CLI), 18 tests, the detectability package, and the user guides in English and Chinese.
